title: Sable and the Cover
premise: Coral Delacroix, a freelance interpreter who quietly handles the delegations and defectors no government wants on record, is pulled back in when a Geneva safe house appears in a real-estate listing — interior photos revealing documents he translated years ago. The listing is bait, set by a broker named Sable who trades in people's pasts, and the prize is Ilse Brandt, a Frankfurt-bound defector whose testimony could move markets before opening bell. Coral must decide whether Ilse is a witness or the lure, assembling an improvised family of burned handlers and a teenage hacker to get her out. In the end Coral exposes Sable's ledger publicly, sacrificing his own anonymity, and chooses to keep the found family rather than vanish again.
about_author: Mara Winterbourne is the pen name of a former conference interpreter who spent a decade in rooms where nothing was ever minuted. She writes thrillers about the people paid to be invisible.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Scrolling property listings at 2 a.m., he recognizes the safe house from a 2019 extraction — same scuffed floor, same hidden cabinet visible in photo eleven. Emotional beat: cold dread; someone is selling his secrets back to him.

chapters.title: Cases No One Wants Attributed
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, flashback-woven. Establishes his trade: unattributed interpretation for delegations designed to fail gracefully. He burns his old contact card. Beat: weary professionalism masking loneliness.

chapters.title: The Buyer's Agent
chapters.summary: Coral meets 'Sable' at an open house that isn't an open house. Sable knows his real name, his mother's maiden language, his last three aliases. Beat: the hunter realizing he has been catalogued.

chapters.title: Frankfurt Opens at Nine
chapters.summary: Handler Marguerite Osei's POV. She recruits Coral: defector Ilse Brandt carries evidence that will crater two banks at market open. Timeline pressure established. Beat: reluctant re-entry into the game.

chapters.title: Ilse
chapters.summary: Coral interviews Ilse in a Rotterdam hotel. Brilliant, frightened, oddly serene — she expected him. She asks what he was paid for her predecessor's file. Beat: suspicion blooming into uneasy respect.

chapters.title: Bait or Witness
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Internal briefing leaks suggest Ilse may be deliberately dangled by Sable's network. Marguerite orders Coral to proceed anyway. Beat: moral compromise as standard operating procedure.

chapters.title: Photo Eleven
chapters.summary: Coral traces the listing photographer to a shuttered studio in Antwerp. Finds negatives of a dozen safe houses — including one currently housing Ilse. Beat: the trap is already sprung.

chapters.title: The Teenager Who Reads Metadata
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. He tracks down Noor, a seventeen-year-old hacker who once scrubbed his digital trail, and offers her the only currency he has: honesty. Beat: first thread of found family.

chapters.title: Rotterdam Moves
chapters.summary: Assassins hit the hotel twenty minutes after checkout. Coral and Ilse escape through service corridors while Noor reroutes their phones. Beat: kinetic fear; trust forged under fire.

chapters.title: Sable's Terms
chapters.summary: A phone call. Sable offers Coral his old life back — full erasure — if he delivers Ilse alone. Beat: temptation articulated perfectly, which makes it worse.

chapters.title: What Ilse Carries
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. She reveals she isn't just carrying documents; she memorized them and burned the originals, so only she can testify. Beat: agency reclaimed; she is the asset, not the luggage.

chapters.title: Marguerite's Ledger
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. We learn she has been feeding Sable selective truths for years to protect her own people. Beat: the protector with blood on her hands.

chapters.title: Night Train to Basel
chapters.summary: Coral, Ilse, and Noor travel under cover of a pharmaceutical delegation Coral once interpreted for. He translates small kindnesses between strangers. Beat: tenderness inside tradecraft.

chapters.title: The Interpreter's Dilemma
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, reflective. He confesses to Ilse that he once mistranslated on purpose to save a life — and got three others killed. Beat: guilt offered like a hand extended.

chapters.title: Basel Station
chapters.summary: A meet goes wrong; Marguerite's courier is Sable's man. The team scatters. Noor is briefly taken and released with a tracker she pretends not to know about. Beat: betrayal reshuffles every alliance.

chapters.title: Noor's Choice
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. She tells the team about the tracker herself, then uses it to feed false positioning. Beat: the kid becomes indispensable; belonging earned through candor.

chapters.title: The House That Was Sold Twice
chapters.summary: Coral returns to the listed safe house and finds it staged — furniture arranged like the photos, waiting for a buyer who is really an assassin. He leaves a message in the cabinet. Beat: turning predator-ward.

chapters.title: Markets Nervous
chapters.summary: Financial-world interlude, multiple minor POVs. Rumors of the defector move bond spreads. Beat: the clock tightening; abstract stakes made concrete.

chapters.title: Marguerite Calls It Off
chapters.summary: Marguerite orders abort: exposure risk too high. Coral refuses, going off-book with Ilse and Noor. Beat: severance from institutional protection; found family formalized.

chapters.title: Ghost Protocol, Improvised
chapters.summary: The trio builds a route to Frankfurt using dead interpreter protocols Coral invented years ago. Beat: competence porn; hope with edges.

chapters.title: Sable's Origin
chapters.summary: Interleaved chapters reveal Sable was once a translator too, erased by the same machine that made Coral. Beat: mirror-image villainy; Coral sees his possible future.

chapters.title: The Safe Apartment
chapters.summary: One quiet night in a Frankfurt suburb: groceries, bad television, Ilse teaching Noor German idioms. Beat: the calm before; family almost believable.

chapters.title: Tail
chapters.summary: Coral spots surveillance outside the apartment — but it's Marguerite, off-book herself, warning that Sable bought the building. Beat: ally returns, trap confirmed.

chapters.title: Extraction Plan C
chapters.summary: Planning chapter. They will move Ilse during pre-market hours through the financial district itself, hiding her among the crowd of suits. Beat: audacity as strategy.

chapters.title: The Cabinet Message Answered
chapters.summary: Sable replies to Coral's note: a meeting, neutral ground, no weapons. Coral goes, against everyone's advice. Beat: confrontation of doubles.

chapters.title: Two Translators
chapters.summary: Coral and Sable talk across a café table, each fluent in the other's silences. Sable reveals the listing was never about the house — it was a job application. Beat: seduction of cynicism refused.

chapters.title: Pre-Market
chapters.summary: Dawn in Frankfurt. The team moves Ilse through the banking quarter as screens flicker with nervous numbers. Beat: tension ratcheting minute by minute.

chapters.title: Compromised
chapters.summary: Sable's team anticipates the route — because Marguerite's old leak ran deeper than she knew. Gunfire near the exchange. Beat: plan collapsing; loyalty tested.

chapters.title: What Ilse Decides
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Rather than run, she chooses to walk into the exchange lobby and demand a public notary, making herself un-removable before witnesses. Beat: courage as tactic.

chapters.title: Marguerite Pays Her Debt
chapters.summary: Marguerite surfaces Sable's entire client ledger to authorities, burning her own career to buy the team minutes. Beat: redemption priced correctly.

chapters.title: Rooftop Above the Exchange
chapters.summary: Coral confronts Sable physically for the first time. Not a fight — a negotiation conducted in three languages, ending with Sable's arrest warrant arriving via Noor's work. Beat: words as weapons; climax begins.

chapters.title: Opening Bell
chapters.summary: As markets open, Ilse's testimony reaches regulators; the crash Sable engineered is blunted into a controlled fall. Beat: climax resolving into consequence.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Interrogation Room
chapters.summary: Coral gives a statement that carefully omits Noor and Marguerite, finally lying for love instead of employers. Beat: identity remade through chosen silence.

chapters.title: The Listing Removed
chapters.summary: The safe house listing vanishes; the house itself is bought anonymously — by Marguerite, as a refuge. Beat: irony turned warm.

chapters.title: Noor's Real Name
chapters.summary: Noor decides to keep her alias even though she no longer needs it — it's the self this family knows. Beat: identity as chosen, not assigned.

chapters.title: Ilse Departs
chapters.summary: Ilse enters protective custody, leaving Coral a note in four languages: 'You translated me faithfully.' Beat: grief braided with gratitude.

chapters.title: Sable's Last Translation
chapters.summary: From detention, Sable sends Coral one final document — proof of another listing, another hunt — entrusting him with the work. Beat: ambiguous inheritance.

chapters.title: The Open House
chapters.summary: The team gathers in the newly bought safe house, absurdly hosting an actual open house as cover for a reunion. Beat: domesticity won at cost.

chapters.title: Attribution
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. A delegation requests him by name — the first time his work is ever credited. He signs. Beat: belonging achieved through visibility.

chapters.title: Sable and the Cover
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Coral's voice. He reflects that every cover story is a door left slightly open for someone who might come home. The family sets the table. Beat: quiet resolution; the found family holds.
